item.title: Vice City Girl: JT Is Taking Over ‘GTA 6’ As A Radio Host
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: The City Cinderella is taking her talents to GTA 6, as JT is confirmed to be a radio host in the highly anticipated video game. JT has been doing her big one in the rap game, from her early success alongside former group member Yung Miami as the city Girls to her growing solo career. […]
item.content:encoded:
The City Cinderella is taking her talents to GTA 6, as JT is confirmed to be a radio host in the highly anticipated video game.

JT has been doing her big one in the rap game, from her early success alongside former group member Yung Miami as the city Girls to her growing solo career.

Back in 2024, the Miami rapper silenced critics with the release of her debut solo project, City Cinderella, and delivered exactly what fans wanted. With standout like “OKAY” and “JT Coming,” she proved she could hold her own as a solo act.

Now, she’s stepping into a new lane outside of music.

With the long-awaited release of GTA 6, fans have been eager to discover everything Rockstar Games has packed into the latest installment. From its massive map to the inclusion of popular artists and new radio stations, the game is shaping up to be a cultural moment.

JT has reportedly landed a role as a radio host in the game, meaning players could hear the City Girl rapper while cruising through the virtual streets. It’s another major look for JT, whose personality and presence have helped her standout beyond the music.

Considering how much music plays a roles in the GTA experience, JT could become another memorable voice in the game. Looks like the City Cinderella is getting ready to take over more than just the charts.

item.title: Harlem Rapper Vinny Chase Reportedly Passes Away At 40
item.dc:creator: paige.boyd
item.description: Harlem, NY rapper and creative Vinny Cha$e has reportedly passed away at the age of 40. Longtime collaborator Kid Art posted a tribute on Instagram, sharing that he reportedly died on Monday (Nov. 16) from a car accident. “One of the most special souls we’ve ever known, he gave so much to us and to […]
item.content:encoded:
Harlem, NY rapper and creative Vinny Cha$e has reportedly passed away at the age of 40.

Longtime collaborator Kid Art posted a tribute on Instagram, sharing that he reportedly died on Monday (Nov. 16) from a car accident. “One of the most special souls we’ve ever known, he gave so much to us and to the game. A true pioneer, his talent, charisma, and style helped shape many careers and became a blueprint for so much of what you see today. Iykyk,” he shared.

A subsequent IG post said a small funeral will be held in Pennsylvania on Thursday, and that a gathering will also be held in Manhattan this weekend.

Born Lanelle M. Hector, Vinny Cha$e (who also rapped as V. Cha$e) was a member of the Cheer$ Club collective, specializing in film, music, and fashion. He got his start as a director, shooting music videos and documentaries for the likes of Juelz Santana, Kid Cudi and more.

Switching over to the music side, he released his debut mixtape, The Plaza, in 2011. He has consistently dropped music over the next decade and a half with Cheer$ Club affiliates. The collective’s most recent project, CHEERS CLUB LISTENING SESSION Vol. 1 (Live From The Mercer), just dropped a week prior to his death.

“He took a chance on this dream, and people connected to what we made,” Kid Art said in his IG post. “After finally releasing some music again, we’re grateful his fans got one last glimpse of his gift before he left.”

Kid Art concludes, “This has rocked us to our core. We’ll carry his legacy forward and let his spirit make us better. Thank you for all the love. We love you forever, brother.”

item.title: Looze Cannon: The Detroit Rapper Behind Big Michael Michael
item.dc:creator: T.E. Thomas
item.description: Looze Cannon went from rejected child star to TikTok sensation with 2M followers in a month. His viral success came from decades of hustle, reinvention, and refusing to quit—proving overnight success is built on years of preparation.
item.content:encoded:
Before Looze Cannon pressed the button that changed his life, he prayed.

“I literally, just before I hit the live button on TikTok, I remember it, I just asked God, I said, if this is where I belong, can I get a sign tonight?” he told host Brianna during a recent interview on 97.9 The Beat. “And when I hit the live button, we here.”

“Here” is a place few creators reach. In under a month, the Detroit-born entertainer known as Looze Cannon gained nearly 2 million TikTok followers. By comparison, it took him two years to build 1 million on Instagram. The numbers are the headline, but they are not the story. The story is the three decades of training, rejection, and hustle that prepared him to be ready when his moment came.

East Side Roots

Looze Cannon’s foundation was built on the East Side of Detroit. He describes a close neighborhood where “everybody was family” and hip-hop lived in everyday life. Rap battles happened at school. Ciphers formed on the block. Kris Kross and Naughty by Nature played in the background of his childhood.

Music was also in his blood. “My father’s worked for Prince,” he said. “My mother sung background for Jermaine Jackson. My mother sung background for Stevie Wonder.”

That lineage connects him to some of the most important names in Black music history. It also explains why his entertainment instincts feel natural, not manufactured. He calls himself the family class clown, a gifted improviser who learned to read a room long before he learned to read an algorithm.

Signed at 8, Dropped Without Explanation

Most artists spend years chasing a major-label deal. Looze Cannon had one before he reached middle school. At just 8 years old, he signed with Universal. Then, right after the first album came out, the label dropped him with no explanation.

For a child, that kind of rejection could end a dream. For him, it became a lesson in how the music business really works.

He did not stop performing. Instead, he reinvented himself as “MC Glenn, the rapping Birthday Clown,” working parties so he could keep earning money doing what he loved. It is a detail that makes people laugh, but it reveals something serious: a refusal to wait for permission.

As an adult, he took a job building cars at a Chrysler plant, a role familiar to generations of Detroit families. Eventually, he walked away to bet on himself. For three to four years, he created content full-time from his basement, logging long hours with no guarantee anyone would watch.

The Move to TikTok

The turning point came from an unexpected source. After hearing advice from artist DDG, Looze Cannon shifted his focus to TikTok.

The start was rough. On his first day, the platform restricted his account. His raw comedy style ran into TikTok’s community guidelines, and he had to adjust quickly. He did. He kept his energy, sharpened his approach, and learned to work within the rules without losing his voice.

Brianna credited him with bringing real entertainment back to TikTok battles, including live freestyle rapping. Looze Cannon, in turn, made sure to honor the people who helped him early. He gave a shout-out to Detroit artist Skilla Baby, the first to offer him performance opportunities.

“Big Michael” and the Character Universe

The content that set the internet on fire was a Michael Jackson AI filter. Fans know the persona as “Big Michael,” and Looze Cannon is clear about what it is and what it is not.

“There’s a lot of impersonators,” he said, “but I’m not an impersonator. I’m just a person who put on an AI filter and is being Looze Cannon.”

His goal, he explained, was to imagine a side of the King of Pop the public rarely saw. “We only know the public figure Mike, but you hear stories about Mike being a funny person,” he said. “So I just wanted to bring my own perspective of what he possibly would be like on his funny time.”

Big Michael is only part of the lineup. Looze Cannon also performs as Uncle Luce and Ms. Bernice, characters that feel familiar to anyone who grew up around a lively Black family gathering. It is that sense of recognition, rooted in shared culture rather than stereotype, that keeps audiences coming back.

A Prophecy on Wax

One of the most striking details from the interview has nothing to do with TikTok. About three years ago, Looze Cannon released an album titled Now or Never. On it, he rapped about Michael Jackson.

At the time, nobody could have predicted that an MJ-inspired persona would make him a viral star. Looking back, he sees the project as prophetic, a case of speaking his future into existence before it arrived.

Now the music is reaching new ears. He has heard his song on the radio. He has also watched Chris Brown dance to his track, a co-sign that carries real weight in R&B and hip-hop circles.

Snoop Dogg on the Line

The support has not stopped there. Looze Cannon shared that Snoop Dogg called him personally to offer encouragement. For an artist who grew up on hip-hop’s golden era, a call from one of the culture’s most respected figures is more than a career milestone. It is confirmation that he belongs.

He was careful, however, not to let the attention change him. He said he keeps a “ground zero” work ethic and prefers to work only with good, humble people. In an industry known for inflated egos, that choice stands out.

Independence Over Hype

With fame comes offers. Looze Cannon confirmed that labels have reached out. His answer reflects everything he learned as an 8-year-old who was signed and dropped.

He is focused on independence and ownership. Rather than jumping at a traditional record deal, he prefers working with private investors who allow him to keep control of his work. The reason is personal: his 2-year-old son.

For him, success is not measured by a single viral season. It is measured by what he leaves behind. Building generational wealth and a lasting legacy is the priority, a goal that resonates deeply across Black communities where ownership has long been denied or delayed.

What Comes Next

Looze Cannon’s ambitions are broad. He points to Jamie Foxx as a model: a comedian, actor, and musician who moved between lanes without being boxed in. He is working on new singles and planning a record-breaking 24-hour TikTok livestream.

He also has a vision for the stage. His dream is to headline a tour featuring Detroit artists, bringing the city’s talent along with him rather than leaving it behind.

To close the interview, he delivered an on-the-spot a cappella freestyle using prompts from Brianna, including “The Brianna Show” and “97.9 The Beat.” He also cleared up the origin of his name. Cannon is his real last name. “Looze” came from his childhood, when he was a wild kid who was always outside.

Positive Energy as Strategy

Viral fame brings critics, and Looze Cannon has seen plenty. His response is simple.

“I just fight negative with positive, you know, and that’s all,” he said. “I never like to exchange the same energy.”

For creators who fear the camera, his advice is to block out the noise and focus on the work. That mindset carried him from birthday parties to a factory floor to a basement setup, and finally to millions of screens.

Keep Creating

Looze Cannon’s rise is being told as an overnight success. It was not. It was a child signed and dropped, a young man performing in a clown suit, a factory worker who took a risk, and an artist who kept creating long before anyone was watching.

His final message to aspiring creators applies to anyone with a dream and no guarantees.

“Don’t let nobody tell you that you a small creator, big creator. A creator is a creator,” he said. “Keep creating and be you.”

item.title: Faizon Love Sued For Allegedly Taking $6K And Ghosting Comedy Show
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: Faizon Love is facing a lawsuit after allegedly collecting thousands of dollars for a comedy show he never bothered to attend. Event promoter Inga Harden told TMZ that she booked the comedian for a July 17 benefit event supporting local businesses in Florence, Alabama. The agreed-upon price was $12,500 for at least an hour of […]
item.content:encoded:
Faizon Love is facing a lawsuit after allegedly collecting thousands of dollars for a comedy show he never bothered to attend.

Event promoter Inga Harden told TMZ that she booked the comedian for a July 17 benefit event supporting local businesses in Florence, Alabama. The agreed-upon price was $12,500 for at least an hour of comedy, and Harden says she paid Love $6,250 upfront to secure his appearance.

Unfortunately, the laughs apparently weren’t included in the deal.

According to the lawsuit, Harden began getting nervous after learning about Love’s ongoing child support troubles. She contacted his agent, Eric Young, through her attorney to confirm that the comedian was still planning to show up. Young allegedly questioned why everyone was “panicking.”

But things reportedly took an even stranger turn 11 days before the event when an attorney representing a woman seeking child support from Love contacted Harden. The attorney allegedly demanded that she withhold part of Love’s payment and warned that she could face legal sanctions if she failed to comply.

Love ultimately failed to appear, according to the complaint, and Harden claims nobody from his team bothered to notify her that he wasn’t coming.

The comedian’s child support issues are nothing new. Love was arrested in Florida in June on contempt of court charges stemming from a dispute with Tiffany Lee, who reportedly claims he owes approximately $250,000 in child support.

Harden says she attempted to recover her $6,250 deposit but couldn’t get anyone to return her money. Instead, she allegedly received a mysterious $1 Cash App payment days later, followed by a text from Young asking her to verify her account. The lawsuit doesn’t identify who sent the dollar.

Now Harden is suing Love, Young and Young’s company, seeking $6,436.50 in remaining deposit money and fees, along with additional damages.

Love has yet to publicly address the allegations.

Apparently, the only thing that showed up for this comedy show was the lawsuit. And somebody was $1 richer.

item.title: Drake Fans Lose It After Hearing His Music In ‘GTA 6’
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: Drake fans planning to spend hours playing Grand Theft Auto VI are in for a surprise. The Boy has officially made his way into the game, and fans are already losing it. Well, not as a playable character, but you can apparently catch some of Drizzy’s music while cruising around in the game. Several streamers […]
item.content:encoded:
Drake fans planning to spend hours playing Grand Theft Auto VI are in for a surprise. The Boy has officially made his way into the game, and fans are already losing it.

Well, not as a playable character, but you can apparently catch some of Drizzy’s music while cruising around in the game. Several streamers have crashed out after hearing the OVO rapper pop up during gameplay, leading to some hilarious reactions.

So far, three Drake records have been spotted, “Hold On, We’re Going Home,” “Nokia” and “Nonstop.” Contributing to a solid soundtrack the game has displayed thus far.

The reactions have been priceless, with some fans clearly not expecting to hear Drake while playing. Some gamers are trying to enjoy the mission, while others are more interested in turning the car radio up.

It has not been confirmed whether Drake will also appear on the official Grand Theft Auto VI album.

The news also comes as Drake finds himself in the Grammy conversation despite choosing not to submit his latest albums for consideration. His contribution to Karol G’s “Ahi” earned him a nomination for Best Latin Song, even after he made his feelings about the Recording Academy clear on ICEMAN.

“This album, I’m never submittin’ it/’Cause I know that they’ll never consider it./This might be the one year I won/’Cause I know how they like to position it,”

Whether he’s chasing Grammy’s or popping up on the radio in GTA 6, Drizzy keeps finding ways to get into the conversation. Check out some of the fan reactions below.

item.title: Offset Says He’s In A Good Place With Both Cardi B & Stefon Diggs
item.dc:creator: O Mazariego
item.description: After years of taking blatant and subliminal shots at each other on social media posts and stories, it seems like Offset and Cardi B might actually be on good terms… at least on Offset”s part. According to TMZ, Cardi B’s ex-husband and baby daddy stopped by Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda’s podcast, The Real Report, […]
item.content:encoded:
After years of taking blatant and subliminal shots at each other on social media posts and stories, it seems like Offset and Cardi B might actually be on good terms… at least on Offset”s part.

According to TMZ, Cardi B’s ex-husband and baby daddy stopped by Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda’s podcast, The Real Report, and when he was asked about his co-parenting situation with the very outspoken Cardi B, Offset revealed that the two are on good terms saying there’s “No issues. We grown adults… everything is sweet spot.”

Well, that’s good to know. He even seems to be okay with Cardi’s famous NFL superstar boo, Stefon Diggs whom Tony Yayo asked if he ever wanted to “f*ck up.”

“Hell naw. Ain’t no hard feelings,” Offset said. “Player to player, hell, I done did that… I’m him.”

Whether or not Cardi B agrees with Offset’s assertion that the two (or three?) are okay with where they’re at in their relationship remains to be seen but as far as Offset is concerned, everything’s on the up and up and there’s no issues to be hashed out amongst them.

Check out the clip of Offset’s responses to Yayo and Murda’s questions about his relationship with Cardi B and Stefon Diggs and let us know if your thoughts in the comments section below.

item.title: Drake Still Lands Grammy Nomination Despite Skipping Submissions
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: Drake is up for Grammy consideration after all, despite choosing not to submit his latest projects for this year’s awards. The Boy made it clear that he was letting the music speak for itself, opting not to submit ICEMAN, HABIBITI or MAID OF HONOUR for 2027 Grammy consideration. He even addressed his decision on the […]
item.content:encoded:
Drake is up for Grammy consideration after all, despite choosing not to submit his latest projects for this year’s awards.

The Boy made it clear that he was letting the music speak for itself, opting not to submit ICEMAN, HABIBITI or MAID OF HONOUR for 2027 Grammy consideration.

He even addressed his decision on the track “Make Them Know,” where he made it clear that he was done submitting his music after years of feeling slighted by the Recording Academy.

“This album, I’m never submittin’ it/’Cause I know that they’ll never consider it./This might be the one year I won/’Cause I know how they like to position it,”

But plot twist: Drizzy’s name is still in the Grammy conversation thanks to a collaboration with Karol G.

Their song “Ahi” has officially earned a nomination for Best Latin Song at the 2027 Grammy Awards. The category recognizes songwriters, meaning Drake is credited alongside Karol G and the song’s other writers.

Despite sitting out the submission process for his own albums, Drake still finds himself with another Grammy nominations. It’s a reminder that even when he chooses not to play the awards game, his collaborations can still put him in the mix.

item.title: NSA Classified Communications, Apple & More Suffer Outages, Cyber Attack Immediately Trends on Social Media
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: Multiple major US systems experienced outages today—Microsoft Outlook, FAA, airlines, banks, and Apple. Hackers hit 178 websites with malicious code. The NSA's classified network also went down. Officials deny cyberattack, but social media suspects otherwise.
item.content:encoded:
Is the United States experiencing a massive cyberattack? Social media thinks so and feels the government is being very quiet about it after a series of major outages.

What in the world is going on? First, Microsoft Outlook went down; then the FAA issued a rare nationwide ground stop due to what was described as “extraordinary circumstances”; United Airlines suffered an outage. Yesterday, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, and other major financial institutions reported service outages, and now, today, more cyber shenanigans are going on, bringing out all the tinfoil hats.

Earlier this morning, Newsweek reported that 178 popular websites were hit by a cyberattack in which hackers planted malicious code, potentially exposing visitors to theft of their personal and financial information, according to cybersecurity experts.

Speaking with Newsweek, Security researcher Scott Helme, founder of Report URI, explained that researchers found “188 infected Optimizely projects across 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, HSBC, Salesforce and Equifax.”

Helme also explained exactly what this malicious code is stealing.

Per Newsweek:

According to Helme, the code could steal payment-card details, swap cryptocurrency wallet addresses, capture cookies and screenshots and redirect older iPhones and iPads to an exploit kit. Researchers could see about $7,000 in cryptocurrency reach wallets linked to the attacker, he said, although they could not determine how many card numbers may have been stolen.

The NSA’s National Security Network Suffered An Outage

But that’s not all that happened today. According to CNN, a highly classified US national security network went down, according to several sources close to the matter.

NSANet, as the network is called, serves as a tool for employees to share classified information. So, basically, think of it like Slack, but for NSA employees.

“We see no evidence that this was a cyberattack,” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said Tuesday on Newsmax. “There is no crisis, or anything like that, for Americans to be worried about.”

Apple Also Suffered A Rare Service Outage

But wait, there’s more: Apple has also suffered an outage, with customers claiming they couldn’t access the App Store, iCloud, Apple Pay, and other software. In a statement to USA TODAY, Apple downplayed any malicious activity, blaming the outage on an “internal update.”

“Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” Apple told the news website.

But wait, there’s more: just an hour ago, energy giant Equinor said it is facing cyberattacks.

Bruh.

The current occupant of the White House, Donald Trump, who is currently overseas embarrassing us as a nation, was asked if he’s spoken to the banks about the outage; he said everything is “fine.”

“No. It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and have all the money, things like this happen. It’s fine,” Trump said.

Basically, picture that meme with a dog in a room that’s on fire, and he says, “everything’s fine”; that’s exactly what Trump’s answer to that question felt like.

Still, and understandably, that hasn’t stopped social media from putting on their tinfoil hats, because it sure does feel like this country is under some kind of cyberattack.

We know one thing: these hackers better not mess with the launch of GTA 6, or all hell will break loose.

You can see more reactions below.

item.title: Cardi B Has A Message For Nicki Minaj’s Barbz Leave Her Kids The Hell Alone
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: Cardi B fires back at online trolls attacking her one-year-old son, calling out jealous fans and referencing past harassment of her daughter by Nicki Minaj's fanbase.
item.content:encoded:
While Cardi B is always “if it’s up then it’s stuck,” kids are off limits.

The rapper took to social media to express her anger and disappointment with online trolls making comments on her one-year-old son Grey. 

Cardi posted a photo of her son during his recent birthday party and an online user reposted the photo with the caption, “The Karma you get for berating other people’s kids.”

Cardi had time so she responded to the troll in a now deleted post.

“Yall such a jealous insecure ass fanbase… Yall even hate on a baby. How you beefing wit a one year old all because the world is in love with him??” she said, Complex reports.

“Yall be so mad when people get praised that yall run wit anger outta jealousy to try to convince otherwise too bad yall tweets will NEVER convince NO ONE that my babies ain’t cute…. IN FACT it only gets your faves kid drag wit the mess (which I don’t even like myself) but yall never gave a fuck about that.. truly yall own WORST ENEMY!!”

She added: “Insecure pink thong grown dick eating man yall been putting this energy since I had my first daughter but play victim when the shit was reciprocated back! And stop wit the berating other people kids shit.. I never attack people for no reason and yall know that.”

While Cardi didn’t initially call out the fanbase that always has issues with her, she did note that a “barb” ––a direct reference to Nicki Minaj’s online fans––have been offensive in the past.

A fan wrote, “No ma’am! You just got Grammy nominations today! These ppl don’t deserve your time right now!! Leave it to God to handle their ass!”

“On my son it can be anytime,” Cardi replied. “gotta remind them the type of pedophile shit they used to do to Kulture? When a whole barb tweeted he was going to climb my fence and kiss my daughter and he actually did climb my fence in LA and got arrested OR when one of them posted them moaning and jerking screaming my daughter name ..Or for 3 years straight trying to paint a narrative that my kid autistic…FCK OUTTA HERE then they come here and play like I can’t play too.”

Another account claimed Cardi was lying, “Wtf if this shit really happened we would have heard all about it.. just lying like this is crazy she demonic asf.”

Cardi responded, “WHY WOULD I LIE ???ooooo they gotta pretend like this day ain’t happened cause yall though it was sooo funny when it was happening…..l can also post the video of a man jerkin off screaming my daughter name in 2019…a pink white ponk …Like please I would never lie on my kids …yall hate the fact that yall been weirdos for a very long time and yall was getting away wit it !”

Cardi included a screenshot of a user claiming he could climb the wall to enter her daughter Kulture’s playground. The rapper also posted a text message thread between her and legal counsel talking about including the FBI and Homeland Security to the troll’s threats. 

Once Bardi B settled down she apologized to her fans during an X Spaces livestream. 

“In 2018, when I was complaining about motherfuckers doing videos or putting nooses around my daughter’s fucking throat and shit? Y’all used to edit pictures of my baby dad doing weird shit to my kid and I used to complain,” Cardi said on the stream, Complex reports. “I used to cry about it and instead of people saying ‘Stop doing that,’ they would get a follow back. Cuz I got receipts on that. I got receipts on everything.”

Cardi shares three children with rapper Offset and one child with Washington Commanders wide-receiver Stefon Diggs.

item.title: D. Jones Killed By Stray Bullet, Family Mourns Philly Rapper
item.dc:creator: Matty Willz
item.description: Philadelphia rapper D. Jones, 42, was killed by a stray bullet during a road rage shooting. He was uninvolved in the dispute. Suspect Daniel Dickerson has been charged with murder.
item.content:encoded:
Family Mourns Philly Rapper D. Jones After Fatal Road Rage Shooting

Philadelphia’s Hip-Hop community is mourning the loss of rapper D. Jones, who was killed after being struck by a stray bullet during a road rage shooting.

The 42-year-old artist, whose real name was Darrell Tyree Jones, died early Saturday morning (November 14). According to NBC10 Philadelphia, Jones was driving through North Philadelphia when gunfire erupted between people involved in a separate confrontation.

Police confirmed that Jones had no involvement in the dispute and was not the intended target.

Investigators say the shooting followed a road rage incident along the 1500 block of West Fisher Avenue around 1:30 a.m. Jones was struck while driving and reportedly attempted to reach Temple University Hospital before crashing his vehicle.

He was later pronounced dead.

D. Jones’ Family Speaks Out Following His Death

Jones’ mother, Yolanda Jones, spoke with NBC10 about the devastating loss of her only son.

“They took my only son,” she told the outlet. “My world is crushed right now. I don’t have no words. I’m so numb.”

The tragedy is especially heartbreaking for Jones’ young son, who had celebrated his fifth birthday just days before his father’s death.

Family members described Jones as a devoted father who spent much of his life pursuing his passion for Hip-Hop.

Speaking with 6ABC Philadelphia, his mother remembered his dedication to music and providing for his child.

Jones, also known as Jonesy, had built a name for himself in Philadelphia’s rap scene. His death has prompted tributes from fans and fellow artists, including Meek Mill.

Suspect Charged With Murder

Authorities identified 40-year-old Daniel Dickerson as the suspect in the shooting.

According to investigators, officers spotted Dickerson driving a Ford Expedition and allegedly firing at a Dodge Ram. Police say he briefly stopped when officers attempted to pull him over before reversing into a patrol vehicle.

Dickerson was arrested and charged with murder, attempted murder, aggravated assault and several firearms-related offenses.

NBC10 also confirmed that Dickerson worked as a mechanic for SEPTA, Philadelphia’s public transportation agency. The agency said it would cooperate with the ongoing police investigation.

Meanwhile, Jones’ loved ones are preparing to honor his memory.

A vigil is scheduled for Tuesday (November 17) at 7:30 p.m. along the 2300 block of North Ninth Street in Philadelphia.

For his family, Jones’ legacy extends far beyond his music. He was a son, a father and an artist whose life ended because of violence he had nothing to do with.

Our condolences go out to the family, friends and loved ones of D. Jones.

item.title: Thirsty XBOX Gamers Are Using “New Zealand Trick” To Play ‘GTA 6’ Early
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: GTA 6 launches November 19. Xbox players exploit the 'New Zealand trick' to play 13 hours early at 7am ET, while PlayStation dominates pre-orders. Both platforms claim record-breaking numbers.
item.content:encoded:
If you want to know how hyped gamers are for GTA 6, US-based gamers are literally changing their console region to head to Leonida early.

We are literally 13 hours away from what will be the biggest video game release ever when GTA 6 goes live, and Rockstar Games shared the global release times for its highly anticipated open-world video game.

The game will be available when the clock strikes midnight on November 19, but some areas will get to experience the game earlier than others.

XBOX has a well-known loophole called the “New Zealand trick,” which lets gamers play a game a day early without worrying about getting their accounts banned.

So if you’re wondering, yes, the trick works for GTA 6.

Here’s how it works via IGN:

Open your Xbox’s settings menu, scroll down to System, and click on Language and location. Change the location tab to New Zealand and hit the “Restart Now” button on the right-hand side of this menu to reset your console. When you come back online, your console will be “in” New Zealand. As a result of this, make sure to buy GTA 6 before you change your console’s location; otherwise, you will have to pay in New Zealand currency.

For PlayStation, the trick does work, but it is a bit more complicated. You will have to create a new account based in New Zealand and buy another copy of the game.

Through game sharing, you can give the game back to your main account, but you will have to play on the New Zealand account until the game unlocks on your main account. So, yeah, this juice isn’t worth the squeeze.

So for those putting the trick to use on their XBOX Series S | X consoles, they will be able to play the game at 7 a.m. ET on November 18, giving them a leg up on everyone else and helping them avoid spoilers.

For those who know, PlayStation has an exclusive marketing deal with Rockstar Games, allowing the company to pitch the PS5 Pro and the base console as the best place to play GTA 6, but XBOX faithful are using the fact that they can play the game early to dunk on PlayStation fans.

We totally understand their excitement.

Regardless, PlayStation 5 is still the dominant console regarding where most people will be playing GTA 6. The game is already the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store history, a claim that XBOX is also making about its digital storefront, putting it on track for a record-breaking launch.

Regardless of the vitriol and “console war” nonsense, it’s still a great time to be a gamer. We are literally hours away from GTA 6; we never thought we would be here.

item.title: Wu-Tang Clan Makes History With Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction
item.dc:creator: J. Bachelor
item.description: One of Hip-Hop’s most influential groups officially received its flowers as Wu-Tang Clan was inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday, November 14, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. RELATED: Here are Your 2027 Grammy Nominations TRENDING: LeBron James Moves Up To #3 On NBA All-Time Assists List Comedian […]
item.content:encoded:
One of Hip-Hop’s most influential groups officially received its flowers as Wu-Tang Clan was inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday, November 14, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.

RELATED: Here are Your 2027 Grammy Nominations

TRENDING: LeBron James Moves Up To #3 On NBA All-Time Assists List

Comedian Chris Rock introduced the legendary Staten Island collective, celebrating their impact on music, fashion and popular culture. RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, Inspectah Deck, U-God, Masta Killa and Cappadonna were joined by Young Dirty Bastard, son of late member Ol’ Dirty Bastard, for the historic occasion. During the acceptance speech, Method Man reflected on the group’s unlikely journey from underground rap pioneers to Hall of Famers. “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” he said before delivering a message to those who doubted the group’s success.

Formed in Staten Island, New York, in the early 1990s under the creative direction of RZA, Wu-Tang Clan changed the sound and business of Hip-Hop with the release of their groundbreaking 1993 debut album, “Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers).” Combining gritty street narratives, kung fu movie samples, raw production and distinctive lyrical styles, the group introduced a sound that helped reshape East Coast rap.

Songs like “Protect Ya Neck,” “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Method Man” became Hip-Hop classics, while members including Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah and GZA established successful solo careers.

Their innovative approach to individual record deals, collective branding and creative independence helped establish a blueprint that generations of rap artists would follow. Their influence also extended beyond music into 1990s fashion and street culture. Oversized hoodies, baggy jeans, Timberland boots, rugged outerwear and the group’s unmistakable yellow-and-black Wu-Tang logo became part of the era’s visual identity. Their Wu Wear clothing brand helped demonstrate how rappers could turn their cultural influence into successful fashion businesses.

Wu-Tang Clan brought that same energy to the Rock Hall stage with a career-spanning performance celebrating more than three decades of music.

Backed by a live band, the group performed a medley featuring “Bring Da Ruckus,” “Triumph,” “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit,” “Method Man,” “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Criminology” and “Protect Ya Neck.” Young Dirty Bastard helped honor his father’s legacy with a performance of “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” giving fans a reminder of Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s unforgettable contribution to the group. The induction cemented Wu-Tang Clan’s place among music’s most important acts, recognizing a collective that not only transformed Hip-Hop’s sound but also influenced how an entire generation dressed, spoke and approached business.

More than 30 years after their debut, Wu-Tang’s legacy continues to reach new generations of artists and fans around the world.

item.title: 6ix9ine Sued By Former Affiliate Kooda B For $150K
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: 6ix9ine is facing legal trouble, this time from a former affiliate who says the Brooklyn rapper damaged his reputation. The downfall of Tekashi’s Nin Trey Gang days dates back to 2018, when the rapper and several members were arrested on federal conspiracy charges. After his arrest, 6ix9ine cooperated with prosecutors, testifying about the gang’s criminal […]
item.content:encoded:
6ix9ine is facing legal trouble, this time from a former affiliate who says the Brooklyn rapper damaged his reputation.

The downfall of Tekashi’s Nin Trey Gang days dates back to 2018, when the rapper and several members were arrested on federal conspiracy charges. After his arrest, 6ix9ine cooperated with prosecutors, testifying about the gang’s criminal activities and distancing himself from the violent crimes committed by its members.

After cooperating with the feds, Tekashi was eventually released from prison, while several of his former associates remained behind bars. Now, one of those former affiliates, Kooda B, is coming after him in court.

Kooda B claims 6ix9ine made false statements about him and is now suing the rapper for defamation. He is reportedly seeking $150,000 in damages over the allegations.

Funny enough, back in 2017, before the RICO case, Tekashi named one of his singles “KOODA” as a nod to his former friend. The two were once connected through the same circle, but things have clearly taken a different turn.

Now, Kooda B is looking to collect some money from the Bushwick tattle teller. What was once a musical shoutout has turned into another legal headache for 6ix9ine.

item.title: DJ Khaled Links With XBOX To Give Gamers Doctor’s Notes To Stay Home & Play ‘GTA 6’
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: DJ Khaled teamed up with XBOX to take on the persona of Dr. XBOX, and he has the cure for what ails you, aka vitamin G deficiency.
item.content:encoded:
With GTA 6 just days away, XBOX has enlisted DJ Khaled to give gamers the perfect tool to call out from work and pick up the sticks.

The super producer teamed up with XBOX to take on the persona of Dr. XBOX, and he has the cure for what ails you, aka vitamin G deficiency.

Because of PlayStation’s exclusive marketing agreement with Rockstar Games, XBOX has to find clever, fun ways to join the GTA 6 excitement without directly mentioning the game’s name.

Right now, gamers can head to Dr.XBOX.com and use a generator that creates a personalized note to hand to your employer (we highly recommend you don’t), letting them know Dr. XBOX is excusing you from work so you can get started on GTA 6.

The latest campaign follows the announcement of XBOX Series X-Bite, a one-of-a-kind functional console that lives inside a 5-foot alligator.

Again, XBOX went out of its way not to tie the console to the release of GTA 6, but if you watch the announcement video and listen to the music, it’s unbelievably hard not to connect the two. Also, we all know that alligators are associated with Florida or, in the case of Rockstar Games’ open-world adventure, Leonida.

Now, even though PlayStation has exclusive marketing rights for GTA 6, that didn’t stop CEO Asha Sharma from locking down a 10-year strategic partnership with the game studio, allowing them to put GTA 6 in the cloud and let Xbox One owners stream the game.

We gotta tip our hat to XBOX for finding creative ways to stay in the GTA 6 conversation.

item.title: Red Carpet Rap-Up: Hip-Hop Shines At 2026 Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame
item.dc:creator: J. Bachelor
item.description: Hip-Hop took center stage at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday, November 14, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Three legendary acts, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte, were honored for their groundbreaking contributions to music and culture. Wu-Tang Clan entered the Performer category, while Queen Latifah […]
item.content:encoded:
Hip-Hop took center stage at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday, November 14, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.

Three legendary acts, Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte, were honored for their groundbreaking contributions to music and culture. Wu-Tang Clan entered the Performer category, while Queen Latifah and MC Lyte received the prestigious Early Influence Award. Comedian Chris Rock inducted Wu-Tang Clan, celebrating the Staten Island collective’s impact on Hip-Hop since the release of its influential 1993 debut album, “Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers).” The group later delivered an energetic performance featuring classics such as “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” paying tribute to the late Ol’ Dirty Bastard.

Two of Hip-Hop’s most influential women also received their flowers during the ceremony. Houston’s own Megan Thee Stallion inducted Queen Latifah, while Remy Ma presented MC Lyte with her honor.

During her speech, Megan praised Latifah as a trailblazer who “opened the door for generations of women.” Queen Latifah returned the love to MC Lyte, telling the audience, “If it wasn’t for Lyte, I wouldn’t know that this was really possible.” The two legends joined forces for a performance celebrating their careers, with Megan and Remy appearing during “Ladies First.” The moment highlighted the lasting influence both women have had on generations of female MCs.

For MC Lyte, the induction represented another historic achievement in a career that helped establish women as a powerful force in Hip-Hop. The Brooklyn rapper described herself as “a B-girl from Brooklyn just looking for my chance to inspire and motivate a generation of people.” She also offered some financial advice, telling the audience, “Build multiple streams of income, because one is not enough.” The induction of Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte further solidifies Hip-Hop’s place in music history, joining previously honored legends such as Tupac Shakur, The Notorious B.I.G., Jay-Z, Eminem and Missy Elliott.

The ceremony will air December 8 on ABC and Disney+, giving fans an opportunity to witness the historic celebration.

item.title: 2027 Grammy Rap Nominations: Cardi B, Ye, Don Toliver & More
item.dc:creator: Matty Willz
item.description: Don Toliver leads with 5 Grammy nominations including Best Rap Album. Drake skipped submission but got a Latin nomination. The 2027 Grammys showcase diverse hip-hop generations competing for recognition.
item.content:encoded:
The Recording Academy has officially revealed its 2027 Grammy nominations, and Hip-Hop has plenty to talk about.

The nominees for the 69th annual ceremony were announced Monday (Nov. 16), with several familiar faces returning to the conversation.

Don Toliver leads all rappers with five nominations, including Best Rap Album for Octane. The Houston artist also landed a Best New Artist nomination, despite being nearly a decade into his recording career. Apparently, the Academy has its own definition of “new.”

| BET Awards 2026 Crown Clipse, Teyana Taylor As Fans React

Meanwhile, Cardi B is back in the Best Rap Album race with Am I The Drama? She’ll compete against Ye, Busta Rhymes, Rapsody, Wale and Toliver for the coveted trophy.

The category offers an interesting mix of Hip-Hop generations. Busta’s Dillagence II, featuring production from the late J Dilla, represents the genre’s veteran class. Rapsody and Wale bring their respected lyrical styles, while Cardi and Toliver represent different sides of today’s mainstream sound.

Elsewhere, Kendrick Lamar appears alongside Baby Keem and Momo Boyd in the Best Rap Performance category. De La Soul and Nas also earned recognition for “Run It Back!!”

| Biggest Takeaways From Cardi B’s Tiny Desk Concert

T.I. is another familiar name making noise, earning nominations for “LET ‘EM KNOW.” Yung Miami also secured her first Grammy nomination as a solo artist, with “Spend Dat” competing for Best Rap Song.

R&B also has plenty of representation. Leon Thomas earned six nominations, while Chris Brown, Kehlani, Jill Scott and PJ Morton are among those competing for Best R&B Album.

Drake Skips The Rap Categories, But Still Gets A Nomination

One major name missing from the rap categories is Drake. However, his absence wasn’t exactly the result of a Grammy snub.

According to Billboard, Drake declined to submit any of his three 2026 albums for Grammy consideration. That includes Iceman, Habibti and Maid of Honour. The move continues his complicated relationship with the Recording Academy.

The move continues Drake’s complicated relationship with the Recording Academy. He’s previously criticized the organization over its treatment of Hip-Hop and even withdrew two nominations ahead of the 2022 ceremony.

Interestingly enough, Drizzy still managed to land a nomination.

His collaboration with Karol G, “Ahí,” earned a Best Latin Song nomination, giving the rapper songwriting recognition despite his decision to sit out the competition with his own projects.

Of course, Grammy nominations wouldn’t be complete without some debate. The Academy’s selections offer plenty of talking points about commercial success, lyricism, longevity and what deserves recognition in today’s Hip-Hop landscape.

The 2027 Grammy Awards take place Sunday, Feb. 7, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. ABC, Disney+ and Hulu will carry the ceremony.

Check out the Hip-Hop and R&B nominees for the 2027 Grammy Awards below.

item.title: OJ Simpson’s Partner-In-Crime In Vegas Robbery Reveals OJ Wanted To Use His Name For His Book
item.dc:creator: O Mazariego
item.description: OJ Simpson asked his robbery accomplice Charlie Ehrlich if he could use his name in his book to make it fictional—a request Ehrlich found absurd given their later co-defendant status.
item.content:encoded:
Need to Know

  • OJ wanted to use Charlie Ehrlich's real name as a fictional character in his 2007 book without explanation.
  • The sports memorabilia robbery happened the same day OJ's book was released, making the timing remarkably suspicious.
  • Ehrlich claimed Joey Ippolito admitted involvement in Nicole Brown Simpson's 1994 murder before dying, though he later recanted other allegations.

It’s been two years since OJ Simpson has left the land of the living and still we continue to learn more interesting tidbits about his life after he was acquitted for the murder of his ex-wife, Nicole Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

According to TMZ, OJ Simpson’s one time partner-in-crime, Charlie Ehrlich, is revealing that OJ Simpson asked him if he could use his name in his book, If I Did It: Confessions Of A Killer, in order to make the book a fictitious affair.

OJ couldn’t just come up with a random name? How unimaginative was that man?

In a preview for Peacock’s upcoming OJ’s Accomplice, the man who helped OJ Simpson rob a Las Vegas Sports Memorabilia spot in 2007 says that OJ ran the idea by him and asked if he’d have an issue with it to which Charlie replied “‘Well, not really, but I do. I mean, couldn’t you say Lou or Fred or Tony?'”

Exactly. All the names in the world and OJ wanted to use the name of his future co-defendant?

Interestingly enough, OJ’s book If I Did It: Confessions Of A Killer released on September 13, 2007. That also happened to be the same day that Simpson, Charlie Ehrlich and other armed men ran up in sports memorabilia room at the Palace Station Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas, Nevada and robbed the place of OJ’s own personal memorabilia.

And still, the OJ story gets even weirder.

Per TMZ:

Ehrlich previously mentioned in audio tapes obtained by the New York Times that Joseph “Joey” Ippolito was tied to the 1994 murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman. Ehrlich has since claimed he was lying on the audio tapes.

However, in the upcoming Peacock documentary, Ehrlich also alleged Joey’s brother Lou told him that Joey — a convicted drug trafficker — admitted to being involved in the murders before his death.

Ehrlich said … “Do you know what Lou told me? He told me that a month before Joey died, he took him to Italy … took Joe to Italy. Joe admitted that he was involved.”

Lord knows what really happened that infamous night of June 12, 1994.

As for Ehrlich, he was ultimately sentenced to probation for his participation in the 2007 robbery of the sports memorabilia spot after pleading guilty and testifying against OJ Simpson.

Simpson was found guilty for that robbery case in 2008 and sentenced to 33 years in prison before ultimately serving nine and being released in 2017.

We feel like we haven’t heard the last of OJ Simpson’s life and as the years go by we’ll be learning more fascinating and interesting things that OJ did while he was here on earth.

item.title: Yella Beezy Reportedly Owes Mo3’s Former Manager More Than $478K
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: As Yella Beezy begins serving his life sentence, another legal matter involving the Dallas rapper is making headlines. Last week, Beezy was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole after being convicted in the murder-for-hire case involving Mo3. Prosecutors accused him of ordering the hit that led to the fellow Dallas rapper’s […]
item.content:encoded:
As Yella Beezy begins serving his life sentence, another legal matter involving the Dallas rapper is making headlines.

Last week, Beezy was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole after being convicted in the murder-for-hire case involving Mo3. Prosecutors accused him of ordering the hit that led to the fellow Dallas rapper’s death.

Mo3 and Yella Beezy had a lengthy history of tension, exchanging shots through their music before their beef spilled into the streets.

On November 11, 2020, Mo3 was gunned down in broad daylight during a shooting on a Dallas highway. Six years later, Beezy has been convicted in connection with the killing.

Now, Beezy is reportedly facing another financial issue involving Mo3’s former manager, Brandon Rainwater. According to the reported judgement, Beezy allegedly owes Rainwater $478,200.43 stemming from a 2020 incident outside a Dallas nightclub.

Rainwater reportedly sued Beezy weeks after the incident, claiming he was beaten outside the club, suffered a dislocated hip and required physical therapy.

The case also includes exemplary damages and prejudgment interest. The reported judgment details list a figure of $331,337.42, with interest accruing at an annual rate of 8.5% until the debt is paid.

With his criminal conviction now behind him, Beezy’s legal and financial troubles may not be over just yet.

item.title: No Disc, No Problem: ‘GTA 6’ Preorder Sales Indicate A Record-Breaking Launch
item.dc:creator: Bernard "Beanz" Smalls
item.description: GTA 6 smashes records with $1.18B in preorders from 12.13M copies sold before launch, with PS5 dominating 75% of sales.
item.content:encoded:
Need to Know

  • GTA 6 generated $1.18 billion in revenue from approximately 12.13 million preorders before release.
  • PlayStation 5 accounts for 75% of preorders, securing 9.08 million copies and $880 million in revenue.
  • Most players chose the $99.99 Ultimate Edition over the standard $79.99 option, averaging $97 per sale.

GTA 6 is literally just days away from release, and before gamers hit the start button, Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated video game is already set to bring in a lot of coins.

According to market analysis firm Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already made $1 billion in revenue from preorder sales alone.

Sensor Tower claims that Rockstar Games’ latest open-world adventure has already sold an estimated 12.13 million copies, which equates to $1.18 billion in revenue.

Polygon reports that gamers have been shelling out $100 for the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6.

Per Polygon:

That makes the average price of each sale about $97, meaning the majority of players are opting for the more expensive Ultimate Edition ($99.99) rather than the standard edition ($79.99). All these preorders have made GTA 6 the most-preordered game for both the PlayStation and Xbox stores. Earlier this month, estimates put GTA 6 at just under 8 million copies sold and $751 million in revenue, meaning its sales spiked in a very short amount of time.

Sensor Tower’s analysis also revealed that the game will mostly be played on the PS5, with Sony’s latest console owning 75% of the estimated sales, or 9.08 million copies and $880 million in revenue. That shouldn’t come as a surprise, as the PlayStation 5 is wiping the floor with the Xbox Series S | X and has secured an exclusive marketing agreement with Rockstar Games, allowing them to push the claim that the PS5 Pro, and even the base model, is the best place to experience the game.

That didn’t stop Xbox from announcing it also has a “10-year strategic partnership” with the game studio, allowing the game to be playable even on the Xbox One through the cloud.

GTA 6 Is Hurting The Sales of NBA 2K27

To put into perspective how big GTA 6 is, the game hurt sales across the industry, including its parent company Take-Two Interactive’s other massive tentpole, NBA 2K27, which failed to meet sales expectations but still managed to be one of the year’s best-selling games.

The game’s massive digital success also likely hammers another nail in the coffin of physical games. While there has been plenty of online chatter about Sony and Rockstar Games’ decision to move away from physical media, those cries didn’t stop people from hitting the purchase button in the PlayStation Store.

Welp.

item.title: Report: Philly Rapper D. Jones Allegedly Killed In Road Rage Shooting
item.dc:creator: Weso
item.description: Philadelphia rapper D. Jones has reportedly passed away, according to his manager.
item.content:encoded:
Philadelphia rapper D. Jones has reportedly passed away, according to his manager.

The legendary DVD-era MC was allegedly an innocent bystander caught in the middle of a road rage incident in the Nicetown-Tioga section of Philadelphia. Gunfire rang off around 2:30 a.m. following an alleged argument between two people in separate vehicles.

According to NBC Philadelphia, an innocent bystander was rushed to the hospital after being shot but ultimately passed away from his injuries.

As of now, no shooter has been publicly identified, and the investigation remains ongoing.

D. Jones’ manager, Just Reek made a heartfelt statement confirming his passing:

“I’m sitting here still in disbelief crying laughing and crying some more too many memories flashing in front of my eyes you was never supposed to go out like this I tried to be that big brother protector that you needed and still couldn’t protect from Allah’s will. I can’t believe it don’t wanna believe it. It’s good to see you getting all the love you wanted because that’s all you wanted just wish you was here to see it baby boy. I feel like I lost my B.I.G Lifers forever imma be there for mom grandma adon however they need me damn you f*cked me up again.”

Friends and family have organized a “Celebration of Life for D. Jones,” scheduled for Tuesday on 9th Street between York and Dauphin.

Our thought and prayers are with D. Jones’ family, friends and the Philly Hip-Hop community during this difficult time. We will continue to provide updates as more information becomes available.

item.dc:creator: J. Bachelor
item.description: The Core DJs Worldwide Retreat has brought some of the music industry’s most influential DJs and tastemakers to Houston, and two of the organization’s prominent figures stopped by Good Morning H-Town to discuss the event and reflect on a tragedy involving two Dallas rappers. RELATED: Details on Yella Beezy’s New Life Behind Bars TRENDING: Lil […]
item.content:encoded:
The Core DJs Worldwide Retreat has brought some of the music industry’s most influential DJs and tastemakers to Houston, and two of the organization’s prominent figures stopped by Good Morning H-Town to discuss the event and reflect on a tragedy involving two Dallas rappers.

RELATED: Details on Yella Beezy’s New Life Behind Bars

TRENDING: Lil Flip Confirms Pimp C and David Banner Collab on ‘GTA 6’

DJ Tony Neal, founder of The Core DJs, and DJ Hollygrove spoke about the recent murder conviction of Yella Beezy in connection with the 2020 killing of fellow Dallas rapper MO3. Having developed relationships with both artists throughout their careers, the DJs described the situation as heartbreaking for everyone involved.

During the conversation, Tony Neal recalled the history both rappers shared with The Core DJs organization. He explained that MO3 attended one of the group’s events before his death, while Yella Beezy had become a regular presence at Core DJs gatherings. Neal also credited DJ Deuce with introducing Beezy to the organization and helping establish a relationship that continued over the years. Reflecting on the conviction and MO3’s death, Neal expressed sadness for both artists, emphasizing the personal connections the organization had developed with them.

The discussion also explored whether conflicts within Hip-Hop have become more dangerous than they were during the 1990s. Neal argued that rap beef has always existed, but social media has dramatically changed how those disputes unfold. According to Neal, the internet has amplified conflicts by creating an environment where artists feel pressured to publicly respond to rivals and broadcast their disagreements. He suggested that similar tensions existed decades ago, but without social media, many incidents remained outside the public eye. Today, online posts and public exchanges can intensify disagreements and bring additional attention to potentially dangerous situations.

item.dc:creator: J. Bachelor
item.description: Houston rap legend Lil Flip stopped by 97.9 The Box and dropped some exciting news during a conversation with Jala Mashay, revealing that the Southern Hip-Hop classic “Like A Pimp” will be featured in the highly anticipated “Grand Theft Auto VI.” RELATED: Rap Legend Yo-Yo Talks About Her Character in ‘Grand Theft Auto’ TRENDING: Yella […]
item.content:encoded:
Houston rap legend Lil Flip stopped by 97.9 The Box and dropped some exciting news during a conversation with Jala Mashay, revealing that the Southern Hip-Hop classic “Like A Pimp” will be featured in the highly anticipated “Grand Theft Auto VI.”

RELATED: Rap Legend Yo-Yo Talks About Her Character in ‘Grand Theft Auto’

TRENDING: Yella Beezy Found Guilty In Death Of Mo3

Originally released in 2003, the David Banner track features Lil Flip and the late Pimp C, making it one of the memorable Southern rap collaborations of the early 2000s. Flip explained that he initially learned about the song’s reported inclusion through messages from fans. “I got a lot of DMs and I was trying to figure out what was going on,” he said. The rapper also shouted out David Banner, Mississippi and Pimp C while reflecting on the record’s legacy.

Although Flip has appeared in several video games throughout his career, he admitted that the GTA franchise holds a special place in his heart. He recalled spending days playing the game and confirmed that he has already preordered “GTA 6.” When asked how the song placement came together, Flip explained that “Like A Pimp” is technically David Banner’s record, with Flip appearing as a featured artist. That means he wasn’t necessarily contacted directly about the placement. Still, the Houston rapper is excited about the opportunity to introduce the Southern classic to a new generation of gamers.

Beyond “GTA 6,” Lil Flip also discussed his involvement in “Mutant Football League 2,” where he has his own team called the Cloverland Kings. The rapper described the game as an over-the-top football experience reminiscent of “NFL Blitz,” complete with outrageous plays, violence and unconventional gameplay. What makes the project especially meaningful to Flip is the opportunity to represent his Houston neighborhood. He revealed that his team features people close to him, including his son, grandfather, uncle, fellow artists and longtime collaborators.

According to Flip, people represented on his team can also earn money from its sales, allowing him to turn his involvement in gaming into an opportunity to give back to his community

item.title: Summer Walker’s Label LVRN Countersues For Damages
item.dc:creator: Christopher Smith
item.description: The legal battle between Summer Walker and her label, LVRN has a new wrinkle. The label is now suing her for damages and breach of contract, as described in a recent filing. According to reports, the independent label LVRN (aka Renaissance Records) filed a 14-page document in Fulton County Superior Court in Georgia against Summer […]
item.content:encoded:
The legal battle between Summer Walker and her label, LVRN has a new wrinkle. The label is now suing her for damages and breach of contract, as described in a recent filing.

According to reports, the independent label LVRN (aka Renaissance Records) filed a 14-page document in Fulton County Superior Court in Georgia against Summer Walker. It began with firmly denying her allegations of a breach of fiduciary duty, breach of contract, and fraudulent concealment, made in her August lawsuit against them.

The filing asks the court to dismiss the “No Love” singer’s complaint, and then accuses her of a breach of contract and withholding money. LVRN claimes that Summer Walker failed to pay them 15 percent of income from business opportunities they procured for her in addition to not paying them 20 percent of the royalties she received from songwriting.

“Walker has acted in bad faith and been stubbornly litigious, such that LVRN is entitled to recover its resulting attorneys’ fees,” the filing read. LVRN also alleged that the singer stopped paying an agreed upon 7 percent share of the proceeds from her 2026 Finally Over It tour, even though she had initially been paying them.

Summer Walker signed with LVRN at the age of 19 in September 2017, and signed with Interscope on an expanded joint deal two months later. The terms of the deal upon examination seemed to be “brutal”, prompting her to inform Interscope in August that she would not continue to work under those terms, looking to leave using California’s seven-year rule.

Interscope responded in October with a lawsuit against Summer Walker, claiming that her “failure to deliver” five studio albums per their contract entitled them to seek damages. The amount requested is at least $50 million, which would go to parent company UMG.

“Summer remains open to a constructive resolution. She hopes that the matter can be resolved in a manner that respects the interests of all involved, and avoids unnecessary or prolonged litigation,” said her attorney, Keith Moten of the Interscope lawsuit. “In the meantime, Summer remains focused on her music, her artistry, her children, and her fans.”

A hearing for the Interscope case in Los Angeles is set for April 15, 2027.

item.title: Yella Beezy’s New Life Behind Bars Comes With No Privacy And One Shower A Day
item.dc:creator: Stephen A. Crockett Jr.
item.description: Yella Beezy once had the money, the cars and the women. Now, the rapper will spend the rest of his life behind bars, where even a little privacy is apparently too much to ask. The “That’s On Me” rapper is getting a crash course in prison living after being found guilty of capital murder in […]
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy once had the money, the cars and the women. Now, the rapper will spend the rest of his life behind bars, where even a little privacy is apparently too much to ask.

The “That’s On Me” rapper is getting a crash course in prison living after being found guilty of capital murder in the 2020 killing of fellow Dallas rapper Mo3. And according to TMZ, which obtained the facility’s handbook, Beezy’s new reality comes with some pretty strict rules.

For starters, forget conjugal visits. Beezy will either live in a cell or a dormitory, gets just one shower per day and can wear only his boxers while bathing. He’ll also have to squeeze his personal belongings into a small storage box.

Family and friends can visit in person, but they’re limited to one visit per week, lasting just two hours.

And for anyone hoping to get a little romantic with the rapper, don’t get too excited. TMZ reports that romantic partners are permitted to visit, but physical contact is limited to kissing and hand-holding while sitting on opposite sides of a table. Apparently, even prison romance comes with a seating chart.

Beezy’s shopping options will also be considerably less glamorous than his former lifestyle. Depending on his offender classification, he’ll be allowed to spend between $25 and $85 on commissary items every two weeks.

As previously reported, Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole after his capital murder conviction. The verdict came nearly six years after Mo3 was shot and killed in Dallas on November 11, 2020.

Whatever luxury once came with being a successful rapper, Beezy’s new accommodations make clear that those days are over.
